append.text: **Ps 48:2 *Audíte hæc, omnes gentes* → *Escutai isto, todas as nações*** — the bare *Ouvi isto* at the head of a psalm (rule 3), as this row directs; beside D4's *dai ouvidos*. No reader remarked.

**Ps 48:3 *simul in unum dives et pauper* → *todos juntos, o rico e o pobre*** — the place this row named: *juntos* once, with Portuguese's own doubled *todos juntos* for the Latin's doubled phrase (decision `simul`; *juntos, num só* and MS1932 *juntamente, a uma* options). Passed the Latinist twice; no reader remarked.
Ps 48:3 see *in unum*. **Ps 48:11 *simul insípiens, et stultus períbunt* → *juntos perecerão o insensato e o tolo*** (36:38's order).

**Ps 48:8 *Frater non rédimit, rédimet homo* → *O irmão não resgata, o homem resgatará*** (the Latin as punctuated: no question, no second *non*; MS1932's question and DRB's *nor* are options); 48:16 *Deus rédimet ánimam meam* → *Deus resgatará a minha alma*; the noun 48:9 *prétium redemptiónis* → *o preço do resgate*, to keep the psalm's one root (the redémptio note's *redenção* is the option there). Passed the Latinist twice.
**Ps 48:9 *laborábit in ætérnum* → *trabalhará para sempre*** (as this row foresaw; DRB *labour*; *se cansará*, MS1932's sense *penará* options). Passed the Latinist twice.

**Ps 48:9, the place D27 named: *laborábit in ætérnum, et vivet adhuc in finem* → *trabalhará para sempre, e viverá ainda até o fim*** — the two phrases kept two; affirmative, so 9:19's fault does not arise. Passed the Latinist twice.

**Ps 48:11 *insípiens … stultus* → *o insensato e o tolo*** (stultus → *tolo*, new row); **48:13 = 48:21 *juméntis insipiéntibus* → *aos animais insensatos*** — the adjective kept on the beasts so that the refrain echoes 48:11 (MS1932 *sem razão* option).
**Ps 48:13 = 48:21 *comparátus est juméntis insipiéntibus* → *foi comparado aos animais insensatos*** — the row applied (κτήνεσιν). Passed the Latinist twice.
**Ps 48:14 *Hæc via illórum scándalum ipsis* → *Este caminho deles é tropeço para eles*** — the row applied; unknown to the blind reader, kept.
Ps 48:5 *apériam in psaltério* → *abrirei com o saltério* (as 32:2); unknown to the blind reader again; the stylist wanted *ao som do saltério* (MS1932), refused (*som* added).
Ps 48:16 *Verúmtamen Deus rédimet* → *Todavia, Deus resgatará*; the stylist asked *Mas* (option), refused on this row.

**Ps 48:15, 15b, 16** (three places): *Como ovelhas foram postos no inferno*; *envelhecerá no inferno*; *da mão do inferno* — the wicked's fate twice, the psalmist rescued from it once (as 29:4); the blind reader heard damnation first, as foreseen.

terms: | terrígenæ | nascidos da terra (*os nascidos da terra e os filhos dos homens*) | open | Ps 48:3 only (grep); γηγενεῖς, DRB *earthborn*. The image kept; the Hebrew's 'low and high' (MS1932) not followed. The correlative *-que … et* as *tanto … como* was draft 1 — the stylist heard a prose aside, the Latinist (v2, minor) wants it back; option. |

| propósitio | *o que proponho* (the root as a clause, D16's move) | open | Ps 48:5 *apériam … propositiónem meam* → *abrirei com o saltério o que proponho*. πρόβλημα. *proposição* (DRB) was bookish to the stylist and unknown to the blind reader; the Latinist (v2, minor) wants the noun back (option); *o meu enigma* is the Greek's sense. **77:2 *loquar propositiónes ab inítio*** will test it (a plural, after *loqui*). |

| calcáneum | calcanhar (*a iniquidade do meu calcanhar me cercará*) | open | Ps 48:6; πτέρνη. The heel kept, the crux left open (my own slips / those at my heels); MS1932 *perseguidores* and *passos* are options. Passed the Latinist twice. Cf. D41 *supplantátio → rasteira*. |

| placátio | propiciação (*não dará a Deus a sua propiciação*) | open | Ps 48:8 only (grep); ἐξίλασμα. **Unknown to the blind reader** — for Gustavo: the plain option is the clause *o que o aplaque* (MS1932's, the root placáre → aplacar, but *suam* lost). 129:4 *propitiátio* (ἱλασμός) would share *propiciação*. Passed the Latinist twice. |
| stultus | tolo (*o insensato e o tolo*) | open | Ps 48:11; 91:7 (*insípiens … stultus*, grep). ἄνους; kept apart from insípiens → insensato. *estulto*, *néscio* options. |

| vocáre nómina in terris | *chamaram os seus nomes nas suas terras* | open | Ps 48:12 — the Latinist's MAJOR on draft 1's DRB build (*chamaram as suas terras pelos seus nomes*, which makes *terras* the object and explains). Taken; the DRB and MS1932 (*deram os seus nomes às suas terras*) builds are options. |

| depáscere | pastar (*a morte os pastará*) | open | Ps 48:15 only; L&S cites it under 'consume'; the Greek ποιμαίνει is the shepherd. *pastar* keeps the pasture root; the blind reader heard 'death their shepherd' first, the devouring second — both are the Latin's. *apascentar*, MS1932 *fará deles o seu pasto* options. |

| a glória eórum (48:15b) | *desde a glória deles* | open | Ps 48:15b. **The two Latinist runs contradict:** v1 asked *desde* against *longe da*; v2 asks *longe da* back ('a' separative). *desde* holds 'from' and 'since' (MS1932 *passada a sua glória*); for Gustavo's ear. *deles*, not *sua*: two readers heard *sua* as God's. |

| interíre (of a man) | morrer (*quando morrer*) | open | Ps 48:18; the Greek here is ἀποθνῄσκειν, 48:11 *moriéntes*'s verb, so D15's test gives *morrer*; *perecer* (períre) option; 36:38 *interíbunt* (of a remnant) → *se extinguirá*. |

| *non … ómnia* (Hebraism, 'nothing') | *nada* (*nada levará*) | open | Ps 48:18 *non sumet ómnia*; οὐκ … τὰ πάντα; DRB *nothing*, MS1932 *nada*. The Latinist asked *não levará tudo* twice (minor): refused — heard in Portuguese as 'not all of it', a wrong sense. The stylist's best line. Other *non … omnis* places decide locally (e.g. 142:2 *non justificábitur … omnis vivens*). |

| in vita ipsíus | em vida (*será bendita em vida*) | open | Ps 48:19; the stylist: *na sua vida* after *a sua alma* is heard as '(never) in his life'. The Latinist (v2, minor) wants *ipsíus* shown; *na sua vida* option. |

| tibi when God is not addressed in the psalm | *tu* (*ele te dará graças quando lhe fizeres bem*) | open | Ps 48:19 — the one second singular of Ps 48 is the hearer of 48:17 *Ne timúeris*; *vós* would impose a sudden apostrophe to God (and be heard as the nations of 48:2). MS1932 *te*; the Latinist found it coherent twice. *vos* option. |
formulas: | *(Et) homo, cum in honóre esset, non intelléxit: * comparátus est juméntis insipiéntibus, et símilis factus est illis* (48:13 = 48:21, the refrain; 48:21 without *Et*) | *(E) o homem, quando estava em honra, não entendeu: * foi comparado aos animais insensatos, e se fez semelhante a eles* | open — Ps 48; one set of slots for both verses; *se fez* (the stylist's; *factus*) for draft 1's *tornou-se*; *insensatos* echoes 48:11 |
